To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 7α-MeO substituent enhances the in vivo antibacterial activity of cephem and oxacephem antibiotics after oral administration.
the 7α-Methoxy group in cephem and oxacephem antibiotics increases the gastric mucosa permeability and enhances the in vivo anti-H. felis activity in mouse model.
the 7α- methoxy substituent of cephem or 1-oxacephem antibiotics enhances the in vivo antibacterial activity of these compounds against Helicobacter spp. in mice after oral dosing.

the design of orally active anti-Helicobacters.
the synthesis of new cepham and oxacephem derivatives and with the elucidation of structure-activity relationships in the series of these antibiotics.
the in vivo activity of 7α-hydroxylated and 7α-methylated cephems and oxacephems.

the 7α-MeO group is a key determinant of the in vivo activity of cephems and oxacephems against H. felis in the mouse model of infection.

the 7α-MO group in cephalosporin or oxacephem derivatives enhances their anti-Helicobacterial activities after oral administration, probably by increasing the gastric mucus membrane permeability and/or by prolonging the residence time in the gastric cavity.
the 7α-substituent is important for the in vivo activity against H. felis in the stomach, and the 7α-OCH3 substituent is the most effective for in vivo activity.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the 7α- methoxy substituent in 7α-methyl-cephem antibiotics enhances their in vivo activity in mice after gastric administration.
the 7α-substituent of cephems and oxacephems is important to their anti-H. felis and H. pylori activities.
the 7α-MeO group is a good pharmacophore for the treatment of gastric infections.
